system.name: IterIS
system.one_liner: Optimization-based LoRA merging with iterative inference-solving alignment, applied to text-to-image diffusion, vision-language models and LLMs.

content.variant_note: three lettered application cards, each showing two task LoRAs and their merged adapter on real prompts and outputs, plus a small merge schematic at the top left
content.argues: One merging method works across modalities: two separately trained LoRAs become one adapter that does both tasks, for images, captions and chat.
content.subject: Two LoRAs merged by IterIS into a unified adapter, shown on barn and cat images, negative and positive captions, and two question types.

new_tags.name: merge-motif-per-domain
new_tags.what: the same two-sources-to-merged-result motif repeated in each domain panel, split by a dashed divider, to show that a method is general across modalities

lessons.what_to_learn: To show that a method is general, repeat one small motif (two specialised modules, then their merged result) in one panel per modality, keep one colour per source on every label, prompt token and caption tag, and add a tiny version of the motif with the method name as a key.
lessons.suits: Method papers claiming generality across image, vision-language and text models, especially merging, ensembling or composition methods.

evidence: IterIS can be applied to (a) text-to-image diffusion models for multi-concept customization
LoRA-tuning can be effectively applied to various models, including text-to-image diffusion models, vision-language models, and large language models
we learn a single LoRA for each visual concept

summary: IterIS merges separately trained LoRA adapters into one unified adapter without access to their training data. Figure 1 first shows the idea in a small grey strip: LoRA1 plus LoRA2 go through a blue IterIS arrow into a Unified Adapter marked with a flexed arm. Three rounded panels then show the same merge in three domains: (a) multi-concept customization, where a barn LoRA and a cat LoRA are merged to draw a cat by a barn; (b) multi-style captions, where a negative-style and a positive-style LoRA caption a baseball photo in both styles; (c) multiple NLP tasks, where two question-type templates are answered through an LLM with check marks. Green, gold and orange follow the first LoRA, the second LoRA and the merged adapter.
summary_zh: IterIS 在无需训练数据的情况下把多个LoRA合并成一个统一适配器。图1左上用小示意图说明合并，随后三个圆角面板分别展示文生图多概念定制、多风格图像描述和多NLP任务整合；绿、金、橙三色分别对应两个LoRA和合并后的适配器。
notes: Prior kinds kept. The merge strip at the top left is a tinted block without frame or title, so it is not counted as a panel; the three lettered cards are the panels. The check marks are emoji text. Panel (c) shows templates rather than real answers.
